name: Mortęgi Palace
architectural_style: A palace and park built around the middle of the 19th century on an estate with medieval origins, with farm buildings described as older than the palace
accessibility: A restored palace operating as a hotel with a spa; contact the hotel directly regarding specific accessibility requirements.
tagline: A mid-19th-century palace and park on a village estate with roots in the 14th century, owned by the Geiger family from 1880 to 1945 — now a four-star hotel and spa, a member of Historic Hotels of Europe

description:
Mortęgi was a noble village in the 14th century and the seat of the Mortęski family, including two voivodes of Chełmno and Magdalena Mortęska, born in 1554, who founded a boarding school for noble and townswomen's daughters at a convent in Chełmno. The estate passed to the Żaliński family in 1615–1630, then to Stanisław II Działyński; from 1667 it belonged to Stanisław Narzymski and later passed into German hands.

The palace and park were built around the middle of the 19th century. The Geiger family owned Mortęgi from 1880 to 1945. After the estate was parcelled out in 1945 the palace stood empty until 1947, then housed a people's university until 1950. From 1950 to 2013 it held offices of an agricultural production cooperative, with a primary school in 1950–1960 and a kindergarten in 1977–1979.

In 2013 the palace was bought by Alina and Jan Szynaka, who restored its history and that of its estate buildings. Today it is a four-star hotel set in a park, with the Szlachecka Restaurant in the manor house and a palace spa in historic chambers with a jacuzzi, a pool and several saunas. It is a member of Historic Hotels of Europe.

faqs.question: How old is Mortęgi Palace?
faqs.answer: The palace and park were built around the middle of the 19th century, on an estate that dates back to the 14th century.

faqs.question: Does the hotel have a spa?
faqs.answer: Yes. The palace spa is in historic chambers and includes a jacuzzi, a pool and several saunas, and unlimited spa access was included on the rate we saw.

hotel.room_location_note: Rooms are at Palac Mortęgi Hotel & SPA, Mortęgi 3; ask the hotel which building your room is in
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** At Mortęgi 3, near Lubawa, in Warmia-Masuria.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €119/night for a 20 m² Comfort Double or Twin Room with air conditioning, a private bathroom, a flat-screen TV, a minibar and free Wi-Fi, with breakfast, unlimited spa access and one parking spot included; taxes included. Free cancellation applied before 2:00 PM on 24 November on the rate seen, with no prepayment. A rate that includes dinner as well as breakfast was around €188.

**On-site:** The Szlachecka Restaurant in the manor house, a palace spa in historic chambers with a jacuzzi, a pool and several saunas, on-site parking and free Wi-Fi.

**Good to know:** The estate includes the palace and older farm buildings, so ask the hotel which building your room is in. Booking noted that Genius discounts may apply.
